# dsh-remote-access-proxy
**English** · 简体中文
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-remote-access-proxy) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/topics/d
/www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-remote-access-proxy) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
Use DSH (DeepSeek Harness) from your phone, tablet, or another computer's browser.
The plugin runs a small reverse proxy inside DSH. A remote device opens one address with a random pa
th and gets the full Web GUI, without ever needing the launch token DSH changes on every start. Anyt
hing can sit in front: a LAN IP, easytier, ZeroTier, Tailscale, nginx, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel.
Requires **DSH >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0** and **Node.js 24.9+**.
## Quick start
1. **Install**: sidebar **Plugins** → Add plugin, and give it

Switch it on.
2. **Get the address**: open **Remote Access Proxy** in the plugin list, then the **Re
mote Access Proxy** component under it. The top of the page shows whether it is running and the **en

try addresses**. Click **Copy**.
3. **Open it remotely**: on a device on the same network, open the
address in a browser, e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:13337/k3x9q2m7p1zt/`. Bookmark it or add it to the h
a browser, e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:13337/k3x9q2m7p1zt/`. Bookmark it or add it to the home screen.
Nothing needs configuring: port 13337 on every interface, with the random path generated and saved o
n first start. Add a password or limit who may connect whenever you like.
> **Set your API key on this machine first.** Some DSH settings can only be changed from a page on t
he host (subject to DSH’s own remote-access policy), so set the API key in DSH on the host. Remote p
ages can create sessions, chat, and pick workspaces normally.
From the command line:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Stop the corresponding DSH instance before CLI changes and restart afterwards. Prefer the Plugins pa
ge on Desktop; its desktop profile requires that installation’s CLI and the same DSH_HOME.
## The configuration page
- **Status**: running, off, or not running — and when it failed, why and what to do ("Port 13337 is

already in use", "The certificate could not be loaded"), instead of a line buried in a log.
- **Entr

y addresses**: one per network interface, each with a copy button.
- **Allowed client addresses**: w
hich devices may connect — IPs, CIDR blocks or ranges, e.g. `192.168.1.0/24, 100.64.0.0/10`. **LAN a
nd VPN only** fills in every private range in one click; empty means anyone. Connections from elsewh
ere are dropped before a byte is exchanged, and the page tells you the last address it turned away,

so you can add your own device if you locked it out. This machine itself is always allowed.
- **Acce
ss password** (optional): the entry then shows a sign-in page. A signed-in device is remembered for
30 days; changing the password signs every device out. Five wrong tries lock that address for a few

minutes. `<entry>/__rap/logout` signs a device out.
- **Regenerate the entry path**: after saving, t

he old address stops working — use it if the address may have leaked.
- On/off settings are switches
. A save applies at once: the proxy restarts in place, DSH does not.
Access to host settings depends on the DSH version and its remote-access policy. Plugin updates are
managed from DSH’s Plugins page.
## Do I need TLS?
No. DSH 0.2 works over plain http.
- **VPN / home LAN**: HTTP is available, but does not encrypt traffic. Use HTTPS on untrusted networ

ks; a VPN may provide a separate encrypted transport.
- **Internet**: turn TLS on, or put the proxy
behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx, Cloudflare Tunnel).
TLS needs a `.pfx` certificate. A self-signed one on Windows (PowerShell):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
On macOS / Linux (openssl):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then switch on "Enable TLS" in the page, fill in the path and passphrase, and save. Browsers ask you
to accept the certificate once. With TLS the gate cookie also gets the `Secure` flag.
## Troubleshooting
| The page says | Do this |
| Port … is already in use | Pick another port, or close what holds it. Two DSH apps sharing one `da

ta` directory (portable + desktop) do this too — see below |
| These client addresses aren't valid |
tificate could not be loaded | Check the path (relative to DSH's working directory) and the passphra

se |
| Can't read the proxy status | The plugin isn't running: check both the plugin's and the compo
the proxy status | The plugin isn't running: check both the plugin's and the component's switches |
- **The remote device can't connect at all** (connection reset): its address isn't in the allow list

. The page shows the address it turned away; add it, or click **LAN and VPN only**.
- **`forbidden`

on the remote device**: the path is wrong. Open the full entry address again.
[该节后续省略]
## Security
Access control is entirely the proxy's gate:
- **Allow list**: a client outside `allowFrom` is dropped at the TCP level (before TLS), like a fire

wall rule. Loopback is always allowed, so a local HTTPS reverse proxy keeps working;
- **Random path

**: the entry is `<address>:<port>/<secretPath>/`, generated from the OS CSPRNG;
- **Password** (opt
ional): without it the path alone opens the site; with it the entry shows a sign-in form, failed tri

es are slowed and rate-limited per address;
- **Remembered device**: entering (or signing in) sets `
dsh_et_gate`, a signed value that expires after 30 days (`Path=/; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSit
e=Strict`, plus `Secure` with TLS). It is signed with a server secret over the path and the password
, so changing either — or regenerating the path — revokes every device. Nobody ever edits it by hand
so changing either — or regenerating the path — revokes every device. Nobody ever edits it by hand.
The proxy forwards to DSH as loopback (Host rewritten to `127.0.0.1:<port>`, Origin stripped) and **
performs the launch-token exchange itself, holding the `dsh-auth-*` cookie**, so remote users never
see the per-start token. On an upstream 401 it drops that cookie and exchanges again.
The path is the key: treat the entry address like a password. The `access.log` startup line records
h is the key: treat the entry address like a password. The `access.log` startup line records it too.
